name: Mangara, the Diplomat
oracle_text:
Lifelink
Whenever an opponent attacks with creatures, if two or more of those creatures are attacking you and/or planeswalkers you control, draw a card.
Whenever an opponent casts their second spell each turn, draw a card.
blocked_sentences: Whenever an opponent casts their second spell each turn, draw a card.

needs.what: A **per-player ordinal on the SPELL_CAST event**, read at queue time, so a `spell_cast` trigger can say "this was that player's Nth spell this turn" -- exactly what `data["nth"]` already is on the DRAW event. The tally is already kept: `GameState._tally` bumps `ledger.spells_cast[pid]` on the SPELL_CAST fold, and `emit` runs that fold *before* the caller hands the event to the trigger bus, so the post-bump ordinal can simply be written onto the event as it is emitted. `triggers._matches` would then compare `event.data.get("nth")` against `TriggerSpec.nth` the way it does for a draw, and `loader.__init__` (currently `if model.trigger.nth is not None and model.trigger.event != "draw": raise`) would widen to allow `nth` on `spell_cast`. Mangara needs only the unfiltered ordinal (`nth: 2`, any spell); Esper Sentinel in the same family needs the ordinal counted over a **filtered** run ("their first *noncreature* spell"), which `ledger.spells_cast_ids` already records enough to compute -- so scoring `nth` against the trigger's own `filter` closes both at once. This is the whole "a player casts their Nth spell each turn" family: Mangara, the Diplomat, Ledger Shredder, Esper Sentinel, Mystic Remora's cousins and every "whenever an opponent casts their first spell each turn" tax.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Three near misses, each checked in source. (1) `trigger.nth` asks precisely this question and is refused at load: `src/automtg/cards/loader/__init__.py` raises "'nth' only means anything on a draw trigger" for any other event, and even if it loaded, a SPELL_CAST event carries no `nth` key for `_matches` to compare, so the ability would match nothing, silently and for ever. (2) `trigger.max_per_turn` is the packet notes' suggestion for a printed rate limit, but it can only say "first", never "second" -- and it is counted per permanent (`triggers._queue` keys the cap by `(obj.oid, ability.index)`), while the printed clause is scoped per opponent ("an opponent casts *their* second"). At a pod, opponent A's second spell would consume the cap and opponent B's would trigger nothing. (3) The trigger `condition` form -- `{"cmp": "==", "left": {"spells_cast_this_turn": {"binding": "event_player"}}, "right": {"const": 2}}`, which really does compute the right number at queue time -- is the near miss this codebase already documents as wrong, in `carddef.TriggerSpec.nth` and in the `esper_sentinel` gap: intervening-ifs are re-checked on resolution (603.4, `stack.resolve_top`), and the tally moves in between. The opponent casts their second spell, the trigger queues with the tally at 2, they hold priority and cast a third in response; the re-check reads 3, the ability resolves `skipped="condition"`, and Mangara draws nothing where he should draw once. Loosening to `>=` (with or without `max_per_turn: 1`) survives the re-check but then fires on the opponent's third and fourth spells, or fires for a Mangara that entered *after* two spells were already cast -- Rhystic Study rather than Mangara. Only a queue-time predicate on the event is both, which is what `nth` is and what SPELL_CAST does not carry.
